hypothesis: Y029 found bounded retained assignments may worsen churn when drift is fast. Preregister a finite age-gated memory-use ablation to test whether discarding stale read preferences mitigates harm while preserving slow-drift gain.
freeze: Freeze age limits 2 and 4 and sham/full control, all four prior drift regimes, cohort, metrics, and classification criteria before first-use. No picking beneficial thresholds after result.
source: Use Y029 16 identity/cell, seven active key graph, four-way collision, radius-two matching, 8 episodes/seed. Retain exactly nine inactive entries (or fewer).
policies: matched-sham (writes the same nine-slot cache+timestamps but never reads)
age2-cache (only legal preferences from at most 2 episodes ago)
age4-cache (only legal preferences from at most 4 episodes ago)
metadata: Each stored observed assignment includes its last-observed episode index, additional bounded timestamp metadata available equally in all arms; action capacity 7, memory entry cap9 and total identities/cells16 unchanged.
primary: Per regime, per policy heldout churn, legal preference uses, search calls and matched cache writes. For every regime report full and age2/age4 sham-relative gains. GATING_BENEFIT iff age2 churn < full churn in BOTH drift5 and alternating, and its drift1 sham-relative saving remains >=75% of full-cache saving; TRADEOFF iff age2 reduces churn in either harmful regime only; otherwise NO_GATING_BENEFIT. No hidden switch to best arm.
controls: Independent exhaustive 7-node Hall bound each episode
Equal cache writes, keys, timestamps and occupancy across all four policies; no peek at future state
All samples (positive/mixed/negative) retained; one immutable artifact, one full regression
claim_limit: Finite history-only assignment memory age gating with timestamp metadata, not learned semantic consolidation, cognitive regeneration, or accepted-ref mutation.
